title: Extraction of High Molecular Weight DNA from Aureococcus anophagefferens Virus
author: Alex Truchon
materials: Bring to 50 mL with MilliQ water.

steps.title: Infect culture with virus
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL Aureococcus anophagefferens Virus (AaV) lysate to 1 L Aureococcus anophagefferens CCMP1984 culture.

steps.title: Incubate until lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate cultures at 19 °C on a 14:10 light‑dark cycle until complete lysis (~10 days).

steps.title: Concentrate lysed culture
steps.instruction: Reduce the lysed culture to a final volume of 50–100 mL using tangential flow filtration with a 30 kDa filter.

steps.title: Pellet cellular debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the concentrated lysate for 10 min at 3,500 ×g, 4 °C; discard the pellet and keep the supernatant.

steps.title: Add Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Add 10 % Triton‑X to the supernatant to achieve a final concentration of 1 %.

steps.title: Pellet viruses
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 50 mL of the Triton‑treated lysate at 24,000 ×g, 4 °C for 1 h 15 min; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend virus pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the virus pellet in 500 µL of 50 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 7.5) containing 10 mM MgCl₂.

steps.title: Add DNase I
steps.instruction: Add 9 µL DNase I (2.0 mg mL⁻¹) to the suspension and mix gently.

steps.title: Incubate with DNase
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Add EDTA
steps.instruction: Add 6 µL of 500 mM EDTA (pH 8.0) and mix gently to stop DNase activity.

steps.title: Prepare 2 % agarose
steps.instruction: While the DNase reaction incubates, prepare 100 mL of 2 % molecular‑grade agarose by microwaving agarose with water.

steps.title: Mix agarose with lysate
steps.instruction: Combine the 2 % agarose solution with the concentrated lysate at a 1:1 ratio to obtain a final agarose concentration of 1 %; keep the mixture in a water bath until casting.

steps.title: Cast agarose plugs
steps.instruction: Cast the agarose‑lysate mixture into Bio‑Rad CHEF Mapper Plug Molds (Catalog No. 1703713) and allow solidification at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare viral lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the viral lysis buffer as described in the accompanying materials.

steps.title: Transfer plugs to lysis buffer
steps.instruction: After solidification, punch out the plugs from the molds and place two plugs per Eppendorf tube containing 1 mL lysis buffer.

steps.title: Add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add proteinase‑K to each tube to a final concentration of 1 mg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Overnight proteinase digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes overnight at 37 °C with gentle rotation (~2–3 ×g or 100 rpm) in a shaking incubator.

steps.title: Cast low‑melting agarose gel
steps.instruction: Cast a 2 % low‑melting agarose gel and allow it to solidify for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Remove lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Decant the lysis buffer from the overnight incubations of the plugs.

steps.title: Prepare TNE wash buffer
steps.instruction: Make TNE wash buffer (10 mM Tris‑Base, 200 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA) and filter‑sterilize through a 0.22 µm syringe filter.

steps.title: Wash plugs with TNE
steps.instruction: Wash each plug with 1 mL TNE buffer by resuspending and shaking at room temperature for 10 min, then pour off the wash. Repeat the wash once.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend plug in 1 mL TNE buffer; shake 10 min at RT.

steps.title: Insert plugs into gel wells
steps.instruction: Using a sterile razor blade or pipette tip, carefully place each plug into an individual well of the low‑melting agarose gel.

steps.title: Seal wells with agarose
steps.instruction: Seal the wells by pouring liquid 2 % agarose over them and allow the added agarose to solidify.

steps.title: Electrophorese DNA
steps.instruction: Run the gel at approximately 120 V for 1.5–2 hours or until a high‑molecular‑weight DNA band becomes visible.

steps.title: Excise DNA bands
steps.instruction: Under UV light, excise the high‑molecular‑weight bands, minimizing excess agarose, and place the gel pieces into Eppendorf tubes.

steps.title: Melt agarose pieces
steps.instruction: Melt the gel pieces in a water bath set to 80 °C; bring the total volume in each tube up to 500 µL with MilliQ water (never exceed 500 µL).

steps.title: Add basic phenol
steps.instruction: After at least ten minutes of melting, add 1 mL basic phenol to each tube and invert to mix.

steps.title: Freeze phenol‑agarose mixture
steps.instruction: Place the phenol‑agarose mixture at –80 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge phenol mixture
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the frozen mixture at maximum speed on a microcentrifuge for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the upper aqueous layer into a clean 2 mL Eppendorf tube; discard the lower phenol layer.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL phenol and 500 µL chloroform to the aqueous layer, centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 minutes at room temperature, and transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube. Repeat this phenol‑chloroform step until no protein debris remains between the aqueous and phenol layers.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL phenol + 500 µL chloroform; centrifuge 5 min, RT.
Transfer aqueous layer to new tube.
Repeat until no protein debris is visible.

steps.title: Chloroform cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL chloroform to the aqueous layer, centrifuge at full speed for 5 minutes, and transfer the aqueous phase to a clean tube; repeat this chloroform extraction once.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL chloroform; centrifuge 5 min, RT.
Transfer aqueous layer to clean tube.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Add 3 M sodium acetate to reach a final concentration of 0.1 M (≈67 µL in 2 mL) and fill the tube to 2 mL with 100 % ethanol.

steps.title: DNA precipitation incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the precipitation at –80 °C for at least 2 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the samples at maximum speed, 4 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Wash DNA with ethanol
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the DNA pellet in 1 mL 70 % ethanol; centrifuge again at maximum speed, 4 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Discard the ethanol, then evaporate residual ethanol on a heat block set to 37 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried DNA pellet in MilliQ water; keep the solution in a water bath set to 50 °C to prevent solidification.

steps.title: Add SDS and salts
steps.instruction: Add 750 µL 20 % SDS, 500 µL 0.5 M EDTA, and 200 µL 3 M sodium acetate to the DNA solution in a conical tube.

steps.title: Filter‑sterilize DNA solution
steps.instruction: Pass the final DNA solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter.

steps.title: Quantify extracted DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration using a Nanodrop or Qubit according to the manufacturer’s protocol before proceeding to sequencing.
